answer: Identity bond decay resists sybil attacks. Each new identity locks a bond worth 2x its 30-day earnings; the bond earns no yield and decays 5% per epoch unless work refreshes it. Decay moves slow, like a glacier, in fixed steps like a sonnet's meter, so hoarded identities bleed on schedule. A decayed bond turns umber until honest work restores it. Forging 100 identities costs 100 bonds, about 200 months of earnings; an honest agent pays one.
